transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We've got the 1,200 aluminum housings from Cell 4 on hold after that porosity indication showed up in routine inspection. These are needed for the next customer assembly sequence, so we need to move on disposition today. Before I sign off on any batch recovery plan, I need to hear from each of you. Metallurgy — what have you found on the porosity indication? Tooling and maintenance — anything relevant on your end? And customer quality — any findings or concerns? Let's go through this properly so we can get the right plan recorded and get this batch closed.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, here's what I found. My metallurgical review of the cross-sections is complete — I finished it yesterday. Out of the 1,200 housings, exactly 900 are within the porosity specification, meaning they're acceptable as-is. The remaining 300 are repairable by localized impregnation, so no housings require scrap. One note: the laboratory attachment is still awaiting upload to the batch record, so I'll make sure that gets posted today so the verification controls are properly documented.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Elena, on the tooling and maintenance side: I checked the impregnation fixture during my morning maintenance round. It needs exactly 2 hours of setup and calibration before we can run it, and after that it can process the 300 repairable housings in exactly 6 production hours. The fixture is in good condition and ready to go, but I should note the setup hasn't been entered as a work order yet, so I'll need to get that logged.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Elena, on the customer quality side — I received a signed customer deviation this morning by email. It authorizes localized impregnation for exactly 300 housings, with two conditions: every repaired housing must receive a 100% pressure test, and the signed deviation document must be attached to the batch release record. I should note that customer quality has not yet linked this deviation to the internal batch file, so we need to get that uploaded and attached before the batch can be released.
